title: workbench-samples: lightweight adapters & cookbook for Next.js / FastAPI / Go HTTP / CLI
creator: Priya Narang
description: Create a set of opinionated, lightweight starter templates and cookbook snippets demonstrating best-practice SDK usage across TypeScript (Next.js), Python (FastAPI), Go (HTTP server), and a cross-platform CLI. Emphasize streaming ergonomics, retry/backoff patterns, simple telemetry hooks, and low-friction local dev setup.
acceptance_criteria: Starter repo for Next.js demonstrating generation + streaming with client-side fallback to polling
FastAPI example showing sync/async endpoints, request-level retries, and server-side streaming proxy
Go HTTP server minimal example (single-file) with robust retry wrapper and graceful shutdown handling for stream consumption
CLI example (TS or Go) that supports sync generation, streaming tail, --retries flag, and exit codes for CI
Cookbook snippets (5) for common patterns: exponential backoff+jitter, safe streaming parsing, prefix caching guidance, batching config, and predictable token estimation
README for each starter with local run steps, environment var examples, and one-liner deploy notes
Automated tests (smoke) that validate basic generation + simulated transient failures to exercise retry logic
Links to corresponding PRs and design doc included in ticket comments
tasks: design: propose file layouts and example API surface for each starter
implement: Next.js demo with client & server components (stream + polling fallback)
implement: FastAPI app with sync and async handlers and streaming proxy
implement: Go single-file HTTP example and CLI binary with retry wrapper
cookbook: write snippets and short explanations (<=150 words each)
tests: add simple pytest / jest / go test smoke checks
docs: produce README and add quickstart badges
polish: CI job to run smoke tests on PRs and add linter configs
